cells.tense: You are here at the table with the shape of another person's situation clear in front of you.
cells.ask: Tell someone one true thing you notice about how they are doing, then stop and let it stand.
cells.core:
You can hold someone's situation as a pattern and still stay in the room with them. The shape of it is clear to you — what's underneath, how the pieces move — and you don't need the story or the blame to stay close. That's the rare part. Most people either get lost in the details or float above them. You're doing neither.

The recognition is alive at this table, and it's what makes you steady to be near. You feel with someone without becoming them. They can tell you see them and they don't feel swallowed. Keep the shape you see, and keep the person in it as a person, not as another instance of the pattern. That balance is yours to hold and to enjoy holding.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the shape of someone's life and still stay with them.
cells.verb: feeling with someone rather than only about them — resonance that keeps two centres distinct

cells.tense: You are already bracing for how this will end before either of you has said what it is.
cells.ask: Before you end anything today, say out loud what you are treating as finished, and let the other person answer whether it is.
cells.core:
The pattern has become so clear that the person in it has started to disappear. You can see where this thing is going, how it has to play out, and you're already living at the end of it — and somewhere in that you stopped being able to tell your feeling from theirs. Their trouble is in your chest before they've told you it's there.

Connection without fusion is the thing you're built for. With the boundary gone, a reading of the pattern that doesn't keep two people in it isn't compassion, it's just aftermath. Finishing something is sometimes right. Having already finished it in your head, alone, is the part that costs you the other person.

cells.tense: You once learned to stay out of the feeling, and you are still standing where that left you.
cells.ask: Ask one person a question about their day you don't already know the answer to, and stay through the reply without summarising it.
cells.core:
The understanding is intact and the traffic has stopped. You can see how someone's week is shaping up without it landing anywhere in you, and that's been useful — you don't get pulled under, you don't lose the plot. You read people well. The feeling-with has gone quiet.

Relationships in this register stay on the surface. You are accurate about people and not much moved by them, and the accuracy reads as distance. What's gone isn't insight; it's the willingness to let someone's answer land in you and change what you do next. Small contact, made often, brings the current back through. Nothing has to be forced open.

cells.tense: You are already holding something for someone and calling it only a clear-eyed reading of the situation.
cells.ask: Name one thing you did this week that was for someone, out loud, without explaining the reasoning behind it.
cells.core:
People around you are steadied by how you hold the shape of their trouble. You see the mechanism and you stay with them in it, and that is care, whether or not it arrives as warmth. From where you sit it looks like clarity — the pattern seen, the situation handled — and you'd say there's nothing tender in it.

But the tenderness is what makes the clarity usable. Seeing how something works, without a stake in who it's working for, reads as indifference. This isn't a colder strength than feeling; it's the same care running through your hands and not through your mood. One plain admission, said out loud where someone can hear it, puts the claim back in your name.

attempts.check: The record states others feel your compassion while you feel nothing; what it names is that your care is running through how you hold the pattern of a room, not as a mood you can locate. A reader could rightly say the feeling is not absent, it is unrecognized, and if I am wrong about that, the ask — one plain sentence of what stayed with you — still costs nothing and still tells them something. The line that serves me more than them would be any sentence that flatters the pattern-seeing as a gift rather than a channel; I've cut those.
